body: Evidence (different samples, so treat ranges, not points). (1) Tracker marketping.in (methodology: issue price to latest close; accessed Nov 2026; single-source): mainboard share trading below issue - 2021 44.4% (median +24.8%), 2022 42.9% (+25.9%), 2023 42.4% (+33.0%), 2024 49.5% (median 0.0%), 2025 48.1% (+1.9%); SME - 2023 48.9% (+9.8%), 2024 58.3% (median -20.4%), 2025 56.6% (-11.5%). (2) Economic Times analysis cited by Share India (2026): over 51% of 155 large IPOs (Rs500cr+) listed 2023-25 were below issue price, several 50-70% off debut levels. (3) Client Associates 'New-Age IPO Performance Analysis' (25 VC/PE-backed listings May-2020 to Jun-2025, vs BSE 500, as of 16 Jun 2025): average subscription 48.5x; 17 of 25 had listing gains averaging 24.15%, yet only 36% of IPO-price buyers and 32% of post-listing buyers earned positive alpha (43% of pre-IPO investors). (4) SEBI flipping study (separate record): most allottees exit within a week. Pattern: the median mainboard IPO roughly matches or slightly lags the market over 1-3 years, a minority of big winners lifts the average, and buying on listing day (after the pop) is the worst entry. Issues during hot windows (2021, 2024) fare worst. Consistent with Buffett's 2000 'wealth transfer' warning and global IPO-underperformance literature. Actionable: default answer to any IPO is 'not now'; revisit after 4-8 quarters of listed results unless we have a genuine information edge.
title: Indian IPO base rates: roughly 40-50% of mainboard and ~50-58% of SME IPOs trade below issue price; listing pop fades
